summary: Sprint A end-to-end validation. Backend: 23/23 Phase 2 regression cases still green after the per-endpoint split under /backend/routes/dashboard/, plus 9/9 NEW Sprint A pytest cases (recent-activity 200/401/403/limit, real NAV variation + idempotent 180-count, WebSocket admin/no-cookie/client_admin via localhost:8001). Frontend: /admin renders without build-error overlay, KPI tooltips work for all 6 tiles (AUM tooltip text 'AUM = Σ (principal_usd + accrued_interest)...' visible on hover), Recent Activity panel shows 8 rows with org_name + ptx_xxx…xxxx + relative time + colored +/- amounts (e.g. 'Alemany Capital · ptx_3a…cf23 · 1d ago · +$250,000.00 · subscribe'), 6 KPIs / 3 SVG charts / top-clients / range switcher / refresh all functional. TWO real frontend bugs found: (1) Export PDF throws 'RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView' inside @react-pdf/renderer → no Blob, no download, button never shows 'Generating…' because the error escapes through try/finally without a catch. (2) data-testid='ops-queue-status' is missing from OpsQueuePanel — the header renders hardcoded 'Live · 30s' instead of reflecting wsStatus ('Live · ws' / 'Live · 30s' / 'Connecting…'). WS through the preview ingress is closed before handshake (expected), and the HTTP polling fallback works, but the user has no visual indicator of which transport is active.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking 'Export PDF' produces RangeError: 'Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView' (thrown from @react-pdf/renderer). No download is triggered, no Blob is created, and the button never flips to 'Generating…' (the error escapes setBusy(true)→finally and the React state update is reverted on re-render). Reproduced twice with 45s timeout on Chromium 1920x1080 via the preview URL.

Required data-testid 'ops-queue-status' is MISSING. The header always renders the hardcoded literal 'Live · 30s' and ignores the wsStatus prop. Spec says it must render 'Live · ws' / 'Live · 30s' / 'Connecting…' and never be blank, with a data-testid for testing the active transport.

action_items: Fix ExportPdfButton: the @react-pdf/renderer 'Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView' error typically means a Font.register() source can't be parsed (wrong path, ttf vs otf, fetched HTML instead of binary, or a transparent PNG truncated). 1) Wrap the onClick in try/catch and surface the error in a toast so the user knows. 2) Check DashboardReport.tsx Font.register calls / any Image src — fetch them server-side or remove and use built-in Helvetica to confirm. 3) Verify @react-pdf/renderer version in package.json supports Next.js 14 (some 3.x builds need a webpack alias for 'react-pdf-html').

Fix OpsQueuePanel: add data-testid='ops-queue-status' to the header label and bind its text to the wsStatus prop ('connected' → 'Live · ws', 'polling' → 'Live · 30s', 'connecting' → 'Connecting…'). It currently ignores wsStatus and hardcodes 'Live · 30s' at /app/frontend/src/components/dashboard/OpsQueuePanel.tsx:97.
(Optional) Document that WS through the preview ingress is expected to fall back to polling; the wsStatus pill should communicate that to the user.
critical_code_review_comments: ExportPdfButton onClick uses try/finally with no catch — async errors from pdf(doc).toBlob() bubble up as unhandled rejections and the busy state is invisible because React batches the setBusy(true) with the synchronous-throw setBusy(false). Add an explicit catch that logs and surfaces a toast.
OpsQueuePanel signature accepts `wsStatus?: WsStatus` but never reads it — the prop is dead. Either render it (per spec) or remove it from the component signature.

ws.py: cookie parsing happens BEFORE ws.accept(), good. But after accept the `await ws.receive_text()` blocks on the client; if the client never sends a message we still poll every POLL_SECONDS via the timeout — correct. Consider adding a `finally: await ws.close()` for cleaner shutdown on cancellation.

nav_snapshots.py: the unique index is created AFTER insert_many — if two backend instances both hit empty collection during startup they could each insert 180 docs. Create the unique index up-front (or rely on `estimated_document_count()` + a startup lock) to make backfill truly safe in multi-replica deployments.
recent_activity.py: org lookup is a separate roundtrip; for hot pages consider an aggregation $lookup pipeline or a 60s in-memory cache of org_id → commercial_name.

rca of the issue:
Bug 1 — Export PDF: The pdf(doc).toBlob() promise rejects synchronously inside @react-pdf/renderer with 'RangeError: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView' (visible as a window 'pageerror'). This is the canonical @react-pdf/renderer error when a Font.register source returns non-binary data (e.g. fetched a 404 HTML page) or when an embedded image's bytes are truncated. Because ExportPdfButton uses try/finally (no catch), the rejection propagates as unhandled and the temporary busy state never flushes to DOM before finally resets it; the click feels like a no-op. Mitigation: add a catch + toast, then inspect DashboardReport.tsx Font.register / Image src URLs — most likely a CDN font path is being fetched cross-origin and returning text/html. Quick repro: open devtools Network, click Export PDF — look for a non-200 or text/* response. Bug 2 — ops-queue-status: OpsQueuePanel.tsx line 97 hardcodes `
Live · 30s
` instead of `
{wsStatus === 'connected' ? 'Live · ws' : wsStatus === 'connecting' ? 'Connecting…' : 'Live · 30s'}
`. The wsStatus prop is declared but never consumed. Easy 5-line fix.
